By checking the agreement box and creating or activating an account, you affirmatively accept this version of the Terms electronically. Acceptance is separate from optional marketing preferences. If you do not agree, do not create or activate an account. Keep a copy for your records. Accepting these Terms does not give you ownership of the Platform or guarantee continued access.

When acting for a business, you represent that you have authority for the actions you take and to bind that business to applicable business obligations. If you lack that authority, do not act for the business. Acceptance alone does not create a business role, expand your permissions, or authorize actions for another organization.

sections.title: 2. Eligibility, identity, and account security
paragraphs: You must be at least 18 and legally able to enter this agreement to create an account. Individual events may impose a higher minimum age, lawful identification checks, dress codes, or other disclosed admission rules. You must not misrepresent your age or identity. Nitewide does not supply alcohol; organizers and venues are responsible for alcohol licensing and age verification.

Provide accurate information, keep your contact details current, safeguard credentials and private invitation or recovery links, and report suspected unauthorized access promptly. Do not share an account to bypass role restrictions, impersonate another person, create fraudulent accounts, or use someone else's payment information without authority. You are responsible for your authorized account activity; these Terms do not make you responsible for activity that applicable law assigns to another party.

Organization and event permissions are scoped separately. Membership in one organization does not authorize access to another. Business access may require review, invitation acceptance, and continued authorization. Administrative approval is not a certification of a business's licensing, solvency, safety, or legal compliance.

Unless an event expressly identifies Nitewide as its organizer under a separate agreement, the event's organizer or business—not Nitewide—offers and fulfills the event, admission, package, reservation, and related services.

Organizers are responsible for event descriptions, dates, locations, capacity, access conditions, performance, customer service, lawful refund decisions, and the conduct of their events and personnel. sections.title: 4. Purchases, free claims, and entry passes
paragraphs: Review the organizer, event details, admission conditions, quantity, disclosed total price, fees, taxes, and refund policy before submitting an order. You authorize the displayed charge when you confirm payment. Organizers must disclose mandatory charges and applicable purchase conditions accurately and comply with all-in pricing requirements. Undisclosed terms cannot override rights required by law.

Free offerings use a claim rather than a paid checkout. Nitewide does not require payment information or process a Stripe payment for a wholly free claim, and free offerings do not earn referral commissions. Availability, capacity, and the organizer's lawful admission conditions still apply.

Keep QR codes and private guestlist links secure. A shared invitation may expose all passes on that invitation. Separate guestlist spots have separate single-use passes; a scanned, revoked, expired, duplicated, or otherwise invalid pass may not admit another person. Do not copy, sell, or transfer passes contrary to the organizer's disclosed rules or applicable law.

A booking or guestlist approval does not waive age, safety, capacity, identification, or other lawful entry requirements. If an organizer cannot provide the promised service or wrongfully denies admission, contact that organizer; applicable remedies are not eliminated by this paragraph.

sections.title: 5. Cancellations, refunds, and organizer contact
paragraphs: Purchases are generally non-refundable unless the organizer's disclosed policy, a specific written agreement, or applicable law provides otherwise. Under the Platform's standard voluntary-request policy, a customer must submit a cancellation or refund request to the organizer before the event's scheduled start. The customer is responsible for making that contact, including through organizer messages where available. Submitting a request does not guarantee approval.

The organizer decides discretionary refunds and is responsible for resolving timely requests. An organizer may resolve a timely request after the event, without a Platform-imposed resolution deadline; legally required deadlines and remedies still apply. A request to Nitewide support is not automatically a request to the organizer. Keep organizer conversations and refund requests separate from Nitewide support cases.

Cancelled, materially changed, or unfulfilled events and legally required refunds remain subject to applicable law and payment-provider rules. Nothing in these Terms waives legitimate chargeback rights, statutory cancellation rights, fraud remedies, or any refund Nitewide is legally required to provide. Nitewide does not guarantee an organizer's performance, refund approval, or ability to repay, and is not responsible for an organizer's obligations merely because it supplies the Platform.

sections.title: 6. Stripe, payment providers, and commissions
paragraphs: Paid event transactions use third-party payment services. With Stripe Connect Standard and direct charges, the event business receives the direct charge in its connected Stripe account, subject to its Stripe agreement and the configured fees. Stripe and other providers control their own eligibility, payment methods, verification, holds, disputes, and settlement. These Terms do not change a provider's allocation of loss or remove responsibilities the provider or law assigns to Nitewide.

Each business must maintain its authorized payment connection and accurate merchant details. Do not use another business's account without authorization. Payment-provider agreements apply separately. Nitewide does not promise that a payment method, connected account, balance, or payout will always be available.

Referral commissions are obligations of the relevant business to the recipient under their applicable referral terms, not wages or commissions owed by Nitewide. Eligibility is determined from the configured eligible paid order subtotal and recorded referral terms. A business may set a commission-eligible minimum of at least US $10; combined eligible paid offerings may meet that minimum. Free claims are excluded. Refunds and other applicable adjustments reduce unpaid commissions proportionally and affect sales reporting.

Commission review ordinarily becomes available after the event ends plus a 48-hour hold; this is not a payment deadline or guarantee. Authorized business approval and separate payment authorization are required. Businesses bear applicable payment costs under their commission arrangement. Nitewide does not automatically debit, top up, advance, insure, or guarantee commissions. Previously paid adjustments and shortfalls must be resolved by the responsible business and recipient, subject to law and provider rules.

Businesses and recipients are responsible for lawful compensation classification, tax reporting, withholding, and any required employment treatment. Describing a payment as a referral commission or independent service does not determine worker status or override wage, employment, or tax law.

sections.title: 7. Additional organizer and business obligations
paragraphs: Businesses and organizers must hold all required authority, licenses, permits, insurance, and rights for their listings and events; accurately describe offerings; honor lawful purchase commitments; maintain safe capacity and operations; and comply with consumer, accessibility, anti-discrimination, alcohol, employment, privacy, tax, and public-safety requirements. Providing an address without a saved venue does not reduce these duties.

You are responsible for your personnel, approved managers, promoters, subcontractors, event communications, and authorized financial actions. Grant the minimum necessary permissions and promptly remove access when authority ends. Collect or export customer information only for authorized purposes, protect it, and do not use order or guestlist details as permission for marketing, texting, or unrelated outreach.

Do not publish deceptive events, oversell knowingly, conceal material conditions, discriminate unlawfully, misrepresent commission terms, manipulate referrals, or evade taxes or provider restrictions. Cooperate with reasonable compliance, fraud, support, and safety investigations, while respecting privacy and other legal obligations.

We will not exercise this discretion contrary to applicable anti-discrimination law, protected-review rights, or other non-waivable protections. Termination does not erase accrued lawful payment, refund, commission, record-retention, or customer-service obligations and is not permission to confiscate funds. You may stop using the Platform and request account closure through account settings or Contact Nitewide. Obligations intended to survive, including accrued amounts, content rights needed for existing records, liability provisions, and dispute terms, survive to the extent enforceable.

sections.title: 15. Individual arbitration, class-action waiver, and opt-out
paragraphs: PLEASE READ THIS SECTION CAREFULLY. Except for the exceptions and opt-out below, you and Nitewide mutually agree to resolve disputes between you and Nitewide arising from the Platform or these Terms by binding individual arbitration rather than a court trial. This agreement does not govern disputes solely between a customer and an organizer. The Federal Arbitration Act governs this arbitration agreement. Either party may elect arbitration of a covered dispute.

The American Arbitration Association (AAA) will administer arbitration under its applicable Consumer Arbitration Rules and Consumer Due Process Protocol for consumer disputes, and applicable Commercial Arbitration Rules for genuine business-to-business disputes, available at https://www.adr.org. Consumer protections do not disappear merely because a person also has a business role. One neutral arbitrator may award the same individual relief available in court, including statutory remedies and attorneys' fees where authorized. Nitewide will pay the fees and costs the applicable rules or law require it to pay; a consumer will not pay more than the lesser of the applicable AAA consumer filing fee or the fee for filing a comparable court case. Consumer hearings may occur by telephone or video, or in the consumer's home county if an in-person hearing is reasonably needed, unless the parties agree otherwise after the dispute. Business hearing locations will be determined under the applicable rules with reasonable regard to convenience. If AAA declines administration because Nitewide has not complied with its requirements, a party may bring the dispute in a court with jurisdiction; Nitewide may not insist on arbitration while refusing required fees or compliance.

Exceptions: either party may bring an eligible individual claim in small claims court. You may report matters to regulators or law enforcement. Claims, public injunctive relief, and other remedies that cannot lawfully be compelled to arbitration remain available in court. A claimant may choose court for covered sexual-assault or sexual-harassment disputes as federal law permits. Nothing waives other mandatory statutory exceptions. Either party may seek necessary temporary court relief to preserve rights pending arbitration without waiving arbitration of the underlying covered claim.

For disputes subject to enforceable arbitration, YOU AND NITEWIDE WAIVE A JURY TRIAL AND AGREE TO PROCEED IN AN INDIVIDUAL CAPACITY, NOT AS A CLASS REPRESENTATIVE OR CLASS MEMBER. The arbitrator may not combine different persons' claims or conduct a class arbitration without all parties' post-dispute consent. This does not prevent coordinated individual filings, application of AAA mass-arbitration rules, or legally protected representative or public-relief claims. If the class-arbitration waiver is unenforceable for a particular claim, that claim proceeds in court, not class arbitration, while any severable covered individual claims may be arbitrated.

30-DAY OPT-OUT: Within 30 calendar days after you first accept these Terms, send Contact Nitewide a message headed Arbitration opt-out with your full name, account email, and a clear statement that you opt out of section 15's arbitration and class-action waiver. Use the signed-out account-access form if sign-in is unavailable. A timely submitted notice is effective when received; it does not depend on Nitewide's later approval or reply. Keep your submission record. Opting out does not affect your account, prices, permissions, or other Terms. If you opt out, neither you nor Nitewide is bound by this section's arbitration or class-action waiver.

Other covered procedural questions may be decided by the arbitrator as allowed by law. New dispute terms do not retroactively apply to an already pending dispute without an express agreement.
